goal: Align active gear simulator enhancement eligibility and detail markers with canonical backend facts: socket capacity, item-type enchant options, crafted-only editable embellishments, and the resolver-owned two-embellishment cap.
userValue: Players see only enhancements actually confirmed on each equipped item and can edit only legal sockets, enchants, and crafted-equipment embellishments without a third embellishment appearing usable.
nonGoals: Do not change active Catalog, Gear Release, Manifest, ExactItemInstance, TemplateSet, SimC, PostgreSQL schema, or persisted player/template data.
Do not rewrite or hide sealed source-only enhancements imported from historical/community templates; they remain displayable and resolver-counted.
Do not change target geometry, the sixteen-slot layout, outer scroll behavior, or the legacy pages/builds/detail.js owner.
Do not deploy, run sync/backfill, or claim WeChat manual acceptance in this task's local implementation phase.

currentTruth.factOwner: Backend socket authority and gear resolver own enhancement legality and cap; payload/read-model projection publishes item capability and canonical option keys; Taro renders resolved selections and local drafts only.

mustChange: The active payload capability projection must seed socket option groups for all current-season supported candidate slots while retaining per-item socket capacity as the eligibility gate.

The active payload and formal PG authority capability projections must publish editable embellishment capability only for verified crafted item/variant provenance; partial and source-only crafted records cannot open editability.
The active Taro detail model and design-system marker surface must render only selected resolved enhancement kinds, not neutral eligibility-shaped markers.
Targeted backend/frontend tests and current UI contracts must freeze the confirmed-marker and backend-authority boundaries.
mustNotChange: Do not alter Resolver ownership, its canonical option keys, or the global embellishment cap authority.
Do not mutate PostgreSQL, active Manifest/Catalog pointers, sealed templates, user configuration, timers, or remote runtime state.
Do not add frontend source inference, slot-count inference, a hard-coded embellishment limit, or a legacy-page fallback.
riskUnknown: A raw catalog field may describe an imported/source-only embellishment without proving the current item is crafted; tightened capability must not break sealed exact recovery.
Group-level socket option availability can accidentally look like item-level eligibility unless every consumer retains the canonical socket-capacity gate.
Existing tests may codify neutral marker rendering and require intentional replacement rather than preservation.
evidenceRequired: RED/GREEN targeted Python tests for seasonal socket candidates, per-item socket capacity, crafted-only editable embellishment capability, and resolver two-item cap.
RED/GREEN targeted Vitest coverage proving markers contain only selected enhancement kinds and omit the empty marker container.
Typecheck, UI architecture audit, Harness requirement/verification checks, diff review, and a local CR tied to this packet.
Before merge: candidate-head runtime smoke and the explicit manual acceptance items listed below; after acceptance, merge/push parity follows Harness closure.

ownership.factOwner: server/gear_socket_authority.py owns socket capacity; server/websim_payload.py and server/pg_gear_authority_loader.py project canonical candidates/capabilities; the gear resolver owns final legality and embellishmentMax; Taro and design-system consume those facts.

engineeringHealth.reason: A user-visible simulator capability/read-model mismatch crosses backend and active Taro consumers. TDD, backend-owned facts, targeted cross-layer tests, candidate smoke, and manual acceptance prevent the UI from inventing legality.

acceptanceEvidence: Every equipment row displays only enhancement kinds confirmed for that exact slot; a row with no confirmed enhancements has no neutral medallion container.
Neck and rings retain innate socket candidates, and head/wrist/waist candidates are available only through positive backend socket capacity; unsupported/PvP/zero-capacity items remain blocked.
Enchant eligibility continues to require backend item-type and canonical allowed-option filtering, including non-weapon off-hand exclusion.

Only verified crafted equipment exposes editable embellishment capability; the Resolver blocks selections beyond its published embellishmentMax of two while retaining source-only historical selections as counted facts.
No active pointer, schema, persisted data, legacy owner, target geometry, deployment identity, or remote state changes.

decisionLog.decision: The user approved the Strict recommended direction: backend remains the sole owner of enhancement legality, Taro renders confirmed selections only, and existing Resolver cap validation remains authoritative.
The task intentionally distinguishes editable crafted-only capability from sealed source-only imported enhancements, which must remain truthful display and cap facts without opening new editability.
